clue.text: Read about Blair backing restraint

indicators.note: backing tells us to read the whole assembled piece from right to left
about means the word read goes around the abbreviation for Tony Blair's job

parts.note: taken as written
Tony Blair was PM, the Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Someone studies a story about Tony Blair supporting a policy of restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks as if it belongs to Blair alone, but it turns the whole REPMAD. A damper on a piano or stove restrains.
explanation.definitionFit: A damper is something that checks or restrains, as in putting a damper on proceedings.

clue.text: Difficult to hold an award up, Ms Kerr

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the assembled letters are read from the bottom upwards
to hold means the word for difficult wraps around the award

parts.note: difficult means hard
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: It is hard to lift a trophy, says a woman called Kerr.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' gives HAROBED, which 'up' turns round. Deborah Kerr was a Scottish film actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Deborah Kerr was a famous actress, so her first name fits a clue naming her by surname.

clue.text: Rich king keeps it dark when standing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the letters run from the bottom upwards

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
dark means dim

explanation.surface: A wealthy monarch keeps something in the dark while on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when standing up' turns SADIM round. 'It' meaning sex appeal (SA) is an old crossword convention; 'keeps' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Midas is the legendary king whose touch turned everything to gold.

clue.text: Dear husband no longer preoccupied

parts.note: a former husband is an ex
lost in thought, pensive

explanation.surface: A loved one's former husband is now lost in thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of costly is a synonym of high-priced.

clue.text: High-minded killjoy gets in the way of treating milk

indicators.note: gets in means the killjoy is placed inside the milk process

parts.note: UHT is ultra-heat treatment for long-life milk
a prig is a self-righteous spoilsport

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious spoilsport obstructs the process of treating milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in the way of' is read as 'gets in' the letters UHT.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is morally principled, honourable and high-minded.

clue.text: Experience lower than life

parts.note: lower than, as in under
go means energy or liveliness, life

explanation.surface: Feeling lower than life itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'than' is a link here, though it sits naturally after 'lower' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to go through it, to experience it.

clue.text: Dance with spirit, back half visible

parts.note: rum is a spirit

indicators.note: half visible means only the first half of the word back is shown

explanation.surface: Someone dances with spirit, only the back half of them on view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is not a reversal: only its first half, BA, is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: No-hoper holds false idol to be one who rows

indicators.note: holds means the no-hoper surrounds the rearranged idol

parts.note: a goner is someone with no hope

indicators.note: false says the letters of idol are not in their true order

explanation.surface: A hopeless case clings to a false idol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' makes DOLI; 'rows' suggests quarrels until the Venetian boatman comes to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondolier propels a Venetian gondola with an oar, so rows for a living.

clue.text: Fly in trial upside down over Southeast

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside down means the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a trial is a test
SE is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: An insect appears in an experiment flipped over above the Southeast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside down' turns TEST into TSET; 'over' just places it above SE in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African biting fly that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Flawed agate, black inside, is soaked in boiling water

indicators.note: inside means the letter for black goes within the rearranged stone
flawed says the letters of agate are damaged into a new order

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A cracked agate with a black core is being boiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flawed' rearranges AGATE as TEAAG, and B goes 'inside' to make TEABAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea bag is the thing steeped in freshly boiled water to brew a cup.

clue.text: Cover for sleeper makes bottom grow bigger

parts.note: the bed of a river or sea is its bottom
to spread is to expand

explanation.surface: Sitting in bed all day makes one's backside spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedspread is the decorative covering laid over a bed where someone sleeps.

clue.text: Shy people round the North take tiny steps

indicators.note: round means the timid people surround the letter for north

parts.note: mice is slang for timid people
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Timid folk around the North walk with dainty steps.
explanation.definitionFit: To mince is to walk affectedly with short, dainty strides.

clue.text: Sticky substance makes you fall again

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
fall as in the Fall of man, sin

explanation.surface: Something gummy makes you slip over a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'fall' is a tumble; it is the moral fall, sin, and 'again' supplies RE in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky secretion of trees such as pines.

clue.text: Two boozers getting round us, being uncivilised

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub, a bar
the second boozer, another bar
a round shape is the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two drinkers ganging up on us are behaving like savages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozers' looks like drinkers but means pubs. 'round' is not a container here: it gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarous means savage and uncultured, the opposite of civilised.

clue.text: Sound of car horn that is hard on the chief

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
taken as written
a king is a chief or ruler

explanation.surface: A motorist leans hard on the horn behind the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Honking is the blaring noise of a vehicle's horn being sounded.

clue.text: Stretched up, standing and unfolding

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a road ran across the moor, it stretched
one's standing is one's rating

explanation.surface: Someone stretched upright and stood, unfolding their limbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAN to NAR; the surface's limbs unfold, but the answer tells a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A story that is unfolding is being told or related, as a narrator does.

clue.text: Mixed choir holds onto dead flower

indicators.note: holds onto means the abbreviation for dead is attached at the end
mixed says the letters of choir are jumbled

explanation.surface: A muddled choir clings to a wilted bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' makes ORCHI; 'dead flower' tempts as one phrase, but 'dead' only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is an exotic flowering plant.

clue.text: Sign of island growth

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
corn is a crop, or a hard growth on the foot

explanation.surface: A sign of plants growing on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Fibres working loose in underpants

indicators.note: fibres working loose come apart and rearrange

explanation.surface: Threads come undone in one's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working loose' rearranges FIBRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs are short close-fitting underpants.

clue.text: This type of dog must get wise about America

indicators.note: about means the word for wise goes around America

parts.note: sage means wise
USA, the United States of America

explanation.surface: This breed of dog needs to learn about America.
explanation.walkthrough: A sausage dog is a nickname for the dachshund.
explanation.definitionFit: A dachshund is popularly called a sausage dog, so the word names the type.

clue.text: Red tape cut and decreased in thickness

indicators.note: cut suggests chopping the letters up and rearranging them

explanation.surface: Bureaucracy was trimmed and slimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' rearranges RED TAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tapered narrows gradually towards one end.

clue.text: Worthless money given to Kitty

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
a kitty, a pool of money, is a pot

explanation.surface: Worthless cash handed over to a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' looks like a cat but means a pool of stakes, the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot means cheap, inferior and of little value, as in a tinpot dictator.

clue.text: Most obscure deed unfinished, leading to annoyance

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of deed is dropped

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: The darkest deed, left incomplete, led to irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' leaves DEE; 'Most obscure' reads as an adjective phrase meaning hardest to fathom.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepest can mean the most profound or hardest to fathom, the most obscure.

clue.text: Influence group of journalists in the outhouse

definitions.note: printed as a present-tense verb, while the answer is the past form influenced

indicators.note: in means the press agency is placed inside the outbuilding

parts.note: a shed is a garden outbuilding
AP, the Associated Press news agency

explanation.surface: Sway a gathering of reporters in the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue says 'Influence', a present-tense verb, though the answer is the past form influenced.
explanation.definitionFit: To shape something is to mould or influence it; the past form matches influenced.

clue.text: Re-run bath cured pain

indicators.note: cured suggests the letters are treated and changed into a new form

explanation.surface: Running a second bath relieved an ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cured' rearranges RE-RUN BATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartburn is a burning pain in the chest from indigestion.

clue.text: Work gathered up in time

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces read from the bottom

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
people who gathered met

explanation.surface: Work collected in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns OPMET round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the speed or time of a piece of music.

clue.text: Up in arms freebooter is beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a freebooter is a pirate

explanation.surface: A protesting pirate is executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is beheaded' removes the P from PIRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone up in arms is angry and protesting, irate.

clue.text: Whisper some of Spinoza's ideas

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Murmuring a few of the philosopher Spinoza's thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark spoken quietly so others do not hear, a whisper.

clue.text: One captured by formal King of Troy

indicators.note: captured by means the article is held inside the word for formal

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A soldier is captured by a stiff Trojan king.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the king of Troy in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: A loose pig is running wild, so say sorry

indicators.note: running wild suggests the letters roam into a new order

explanation.surface: A pig has escaped and is rampaging, so someone must apologise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'is running wild' rearranges A LOOSE PIG.
explanation.definitionFit: To apologise is to express regret, to say one is sorry.

clue.text: Wild flower in shadow shot up

parts.note: to shadow someone is to dog their steps
rose means climbed sharply

explanation.surface: A wild flower in the shade grew rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog rose is a wild climbing rose of hedgerows.

clue.text: Lay out fashionable underwear

parts.note: in means trendy
a vest is an undershirt in British usage

explanation.surface: Spend money on trendy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a vest is a sleeveless undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest is to lay out money hoping for a return.
